number.why: The source reports 6 methylprednisolone deaths and 9 placebo deaths, with randomized arm sizes of 61 and 59. These support the served reconstruction for in-hospital mortality within the declared window. The published mortality difference and its 95% CI are on an absolute scale, not the RR scale. Agreement concerns the counts; the held texts do not explicitly establish the mortality analysis as intention-to-treat.

quotes.span: Patients were randomized to receive either an intravenous bolus of 0.5 mg/kg per 12 hours of methylprednisolone (n = 61) or placebo (n = 59) for 5 days started within 36 hours of hospital admission.

In-hospital mortality did not differ between the 2 groups (6 patients [10%] in the methylprednisolone group vs 9 patients [15%] in the placebo group; P = .37); the difference between groups was 5% (95% CI, -6% to 17%).

entry.why: Adult eligibility, hospitalization, community-acquired pneumonia, systemic methylprednisolone and a placebo comparator are established. Severe disease and high inflammatory response restrict enrollment to a subset of the question's population without placing it outside that population. The source describes corticosteroids as adjunctive treatment.

quotes.span: ELIGIBILITY AGE/SEX: minimum age 18 Years | maximum age None | sex ALL

Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted in 3 Spanish teaching hospitals involving patients with both severe community-acquired pneumonia and a high inflammatory response, which was defined as a level of C-reactive protein greater than 150 mg/L at admission.
Patients were randomized to receive either an intravenous bolus of 0.5 mg/kg per 12 hours of methylprednisolone (n = 61) or placebo (n = 59) for 5 days started within 36 hours of hospital admission.
If replicated, these findings would support the use of corticosteroids as adjunctive treatment in this clinical population.
